nodes.label: package-health workflow
nodes.rationale: Checks the shape of what gets published, which the test suite cannot see (#416) - all these failure modes are invisible locally and only bite a consumer after npm publish. Each step runs the package.json script rather than repeating the tool invocation, so flags live in one place and a local bun run lint:package checks the same thing. dist/ is built once up front so the job does not pay for three builds.

nodes.label: publint manifest and exports check
nodes.rationale: Catches a broken exports map, a files list missing the built output, or a types path that points at nothing.

nodes.label: arethetypeswrong consumer-resolution check
nodes.rationale: Catches declarations that resolve for the author but not for a consumer under their module resolution. The esm-only profile is the honest one: the package ships no CJS, so the ESM dynamic-import-only note describes the design rather than a defect - without it the job would fail on a warning with no fix short of shipping CJS.

nodes.label: knip dead-module and undeclared-import check
nodes.rationale: Catches a module reachable from no entry point (dead weight in the tarball) and an import with no manifest entry behind it, which works locally and breaks on a fresh install. knip-bun rather than knip: the Node binary exhausts its heap on this module graph.

nodes.label: bun audit over bun.lock
nodes.rationale: Deliberately bun audit rather than dependency-review-action: that action diffs GitHub's dependency graph, which does not resolve the root Bun lockfile - it records the unresolved range fastify ^5.10.0 and carries no find-my-way entry at all, while bun.lock pins fastify@5.10.0 and find-my-way@9.6.0. That is why the only Dependabot alerts this repository ever produced come from the npm lockfiles under examples/, while the HIGH advisories in the shipped closure produced none. It is also the reason this workflow runs on a clock (Mondays 05:00 UTC, offset from the 06:00 Dependabot window): an advisory is published upstream against a lockfile that did not change, so a push-only gate would not notice.

nodes.label: Baselined advisory IDs
nodes.rationale: --audit-level=high with a baseline of ignored advisory IDs: the closure carries 11 HIGH advisories whose fix is the dependency refresh tracked in #779, so an unbaselined gate would land red on its first run and teach everyone to ignore it. Baselined, it still fails on every new high or critical advisory from day one. Each ignored ID is listed in SECURITY.md and SecurityPolicy.test.ts fails if the two drift, so the list cannot quietly become permanent.
